title: StackAI vs Copilot Studio for Regulated Teams
summary: Pointed comparison: Copilot Studio fits Microsoft-centric IT tickets; StackAI fits multi-department agentic workflows for regulated buyers.
body_markdown:
Regulated teams do not choose an AI platform because a demo answered one question smoothly. They choose it after asking where data moves, which systems an agent can touch, who approves a write, and how the workflow changes after launch.


**Take:** Copilot Studio is fine for Microsoft-centric IT tickets and wrong for multi-department agentic workflows. If your process spans core banking adjacent systems, clinical ops tools, claims platforms, and custom MCP boundaries, and you need deploy-anywhere placement, you are evaluating an agentic workflow control plane, not a Power Platform extension.


StackAI is built for that control plane: atomized multi-agent org processes, low-code builder for ops and IT,[300+ integrations](http://127.0.0.1:8000/integrations) ,[MCP servers](http://127.0.0.1:8000/platform/mcp) , sandboxes/computers/terminals, human review, FDEs + AI strategists, and StackAI cloud / VPC / on-prem with a HIPAA- and GDPR-ready posture. Broader scorecard:[best AI agent builder](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/best-ai-agent-builder) . Agent primer:[what is an AI agent](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/what-is-an-ai-agent) .


## Start with the process, not the logo


A regulated workflow may receive a document, extract fields, check policy, search a system of record, prepare a recommendation, route an exception, and wait for a person before writing anything back. Give each shortlisted platform the same packet, the same destination record, and the same failure cases.


Also kill a category error early. Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio are related but not interchangeable. Copilot Studio is the Microsoft product for building agents and workflows with knowledge sources, tools, connectors, and publishing options. Compare that to an enterprise agent platform. Do not compare a productivity assistant to a workflow runtime.


Personal always-on agents (Muse, Dots) are a third category again: great for a person's day, not your org control plane ([personal vs enterprise agents](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/personal-ai-agents-vs-enterprise-agentic-workflows) ).


## Where Copilot Studio can be the right fit


Choose Copilot Studio when:


-


Your process lives mostly inside Microsoft 365, Power Platform, and Azure-centered systems


-


Your platform team already governs that estate well


-


The workflow is closer to IT service or Microsoft-document automation than cross-department casework with custom tool boundaries


That fit is real. Platform gravity is a strength when it matches architecture. Still validate connector actions, identities, retention, review controls, and network model with security. Familiar brand is not a residency answer ([on-prem and VPC checklist](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/on-prem-vpc-ai-agents-checklist) ).


## Where StackAI is the right fit (and we will say so bluntly)


Choose StackAI when you need:


-


Multi-department agentic workflows with atomized steps and explicit handoffs


-


Tool access across many business systems via 300+ integrations and governed MCP ([MCP for regulated enterprises](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/mcp-for-regulated-enterprises) )


-


[Sandboxes, computers, and terminals](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/sandboxes-terminals-enterprise-agents) for packet work, not only chat


-


Human review with evidence before material writes


-


Deploy-anywhere: StackAI cloud, customer VPC/private cloud, or on-prem ([deployment options](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/deployment-options-on-stackai) ,[HIPAA/GDPR ready](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/hipaa-gdpr-ready-ai-agents) ,[/security](http://127.0.0.1:8000/security) )


-


[FDEs and AI strategists](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/forward-deployed-engineers-agentic-ai) dedicated through first production cohort


That is the buyer we optimize for: defense, banks, healthcare, insurance, legal ops. ## Decision rule we recommend


Use this rule in the steering committee:


-


If the process is mostly Microsoft identity, Microsoft data, and Microsoft channels, and IT already operates Power Platform well, shortlist Copilot Studio and make it pass the five checks above.


-


If the process crosses departments and non-Microsoft systems of record, needs custom MCP boundaries, needs sandboxes/computers/terminals for packets, or needs VPC/on-prem as a first-class path, shortlist StackAI and make it pass the same five checks.


-


If both are true for different processes, run both with clear ownership. Do not force one platform to fake the other's job.


Insurance submissions, hospital referral packets, and bank KYC packs are the usual "StackAI-shaped" examples ([insurance](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/ai-agents-for-insurance-and-underwriting) ,[hospitals](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/ai-agents-for-hospitals-and-clinical-operations) ,[banks](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/ai-agents-for-banks-and-financial-services) ). Microsoft helpdesk macros are the usual "Copilot Studio-shaped" examples. Be honest about which queue you are in.


Also separate search from both ([StackAI vs Glean](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/stackai-vs-glean-regulated) ) and personal agents from both ([personal vs enterprise](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/personal-ai-agents-vs-enterprise-agentic-workflows) ). MCP depth if you pick StackAI:[MCP regulated](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/mcp-for-regulated-enterprises) ,[MCP servers](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/mcp-servers-regulated-enterprise) ,[MCP how-to](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/how-to-use-the-stack-ai-mcp-server) .


## A fair test plan (run it anyway)


1.


**Access:** least-privilege identities; sandbox separated from production


2.


**Evidence:** reviewer sees sources, proposed action, tool results


3.


**Failure:** denied permission or down system stops safely


4.


**Change control:** version and roll back workflow/tool changes


5.


**Deployment:** placement matches residency and egress rules


Measure accepted runs, review time, failed runs, escalations, incorrect write-backs. Ignore polished demo scores.


Coexistence is allowed. Keep Microsoft-centered tickets in Copilot Studio. Put cross-system casework with custom MCP and deploy-anywhere needs on StackAI. Make ownership explicit. Do not pretend one Microsoft bot is your enterprise agent strategy.


If the other confusion on your shortlist is search versus agents, read[StackAI vs Glean](http://127.0.0.1:8000/blog/stackai-vs-glean-regulated) .
